data.title: Sterlite Tech, HFCL extend fall; slip up to 41% from October highs
data.description:
HFCL, Sterlite Technologies share price movement

 
HFCL (₹177.95) and Sterlite Technologies (STL) (₹591.40) were locked at the 5 per cent lower circuits on the BSE in Monday’s intraday trade amid the sell-off in Ai-related stocks globally.
 
These stocks quoted lower for the third straight day. Sterlite Technologies corrected 41 per cent, while HFCL slipped 34 per cent from their respective 52-week highs of ₹1,054.45 and ₹282.10 touched in October 2026. Prior to that, in the calendar year 2026, the market price of STL zoomed 1,146 per cent and HFCL 372 per cent.
 
Currently, HFCL and STL trade under T group category on the BSE.  T group shares are securities that the BSE puts into the Trade to Trade (T2T) segment as a surveillance and investor-protection measure. These stocks are not allowed for intraday trading. T2T stocks can only be delivery based; i.e., the buyer must take delivery of these shares.
 
 

Why are HFCL and STL shares under pressure?

 
STL is a global leader in advanced connectivity solutions, providing end-to-end solutions for building AI-ready infrastructure, FTTx, Rural and Enterprise networks.
 
HFCL is a leading technology enterprise with operations in high-end Optical Fiber and Optical Fiber Cables, Optical Connectivity Solutions, Telecom and Defence Equipment. The company is also creating digital networks for Telcos, Enterprises and Defence Forces.
 
The US markets witnessed a sharp selloff on Friday, with the Dow Jones plunging 949.73 points (1.93 per cent) to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 declining 265.41 points (3.70 per cent) to 6,910.42, and the Nasdaq falling 1,261.47 points (5.28 per cent) to 22,617.73, as concerns over AI valuations intensified.
 
"We are witnessing heightened volatility across markets - equity, currency and metals. While globally equity markets are selling off led by an AI rout, India has been outperforming significantly led by fairly valued large-caps. The dramatic change in the FII stance towards India, rupee appreciation and better-than-expected impressive earnings growth have combined to boost the market sentiments, strongly supported by fundamentals,” said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments.
 
Meanwhile, the significant improvement in STL's operating performance is largely driven by growing contribution from the data centre segment which accounted for 21 per cent of revenue in Q1FY27 compared to 1 per cent in FY26. STL has received a sizeable order of $1.1 billion to be executed over three years for a data center customer and execution for the same has already started, according to Crisil Ratings.
 
Profitability is also supported by the reduction of tariff in the US to 10 per cent in February 2026 along with an increased proportion of sales to the US. The US market typically has higher realisations which has supported the profitability. Supported by these drivers, the company is expected to report revenue of over ₹8,000 crore with profitability of over 20 per cent in fiscal 27, the rating agency said in its September 2026 rating rationale.
 
However, any material increase in tariffs affecting profitability, margin compression due to improvement in global supply conditions, and slower-than-expected ramp-up of the data centre segment impacting overall margins will remain key monitorables, Crisil Ratings said.
 
Meanwhile, the global optical fibre cable (OFC) industry has largely emerged from the demand slowdown witnessed in FY24 and FY25. While oversupply and pricing pressure persisted through much of 2024 and 2025, demand recovery accelerated in FY26, primarily driven by AI data centres, cloud infrastructure, fiber to the home (FTTH) expansion and 5G deployments. AI-driven data centres are significantly increasing fibre consumption, with industry estimates indicating that AI-focused facilities require substantially higher fibre density than traditional data centres.
 
The sharp recovery in global optical fibre/OFC demand in FY26 also led to an improvement in pricing, supporting higher order inflows and profitability across the industry. However, sustainability of this demand momentum and pricing environment in the medium term will remain a key rating monitorable, CARE Ratings said in HFCL’s July 2026 rating rationale. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Wider access to finance, digital economy key to eradicate poverty: FM
data.description:
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said wider access to finance, markets and the digital economy would be key to eradicating poverty and ensuring those lifted out of it do not slip back.

Quoting the World Bank report which showed that nearly 500 million Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, Sitharaman said the Narendra Modi government has focused on targeted interventions, measurable outcomes and tailored schemes to remove deprivations.

"Garibi is not merely a shortage of income or wages. A household without a secure roof, safe water, sanitation or healthcare remains vulnerable even when its income rises. One illness can wipe out savings and push a family back into poverty," the minister said in a LinkedIn post titled 'The Decade India Turned the Tide on Poverty'.

 

She said welfare schemes like Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, and Swachh Bharat are together acting as "insurance against the shocks" that once pushed families back into poverty, while lowering household expenditure and freeing time for work.

"The next phase builds on this progress to lift the few people still at the bottom of the ladder out of poverty, while ensuring those who have already risen keep advancing and never slip back. The protection offered via various measures must now be complemented by even wider access to finance, markets and the digital economy," Sitharaman said.

The government is building closer links between academia and industry through employment-linked incentives, internships and apprenticeships, while the government's investment in infrastructure is connecting the country. Opportunity cannot remain the preserve of a few, she said while outlining the challenges to Viksit Bharat.

Observing that while protection keeps families from slipping back into poverty, to rise further, they need opportunities to earn.

"The government has created financial opportunities through schemes like MUDRA (60 crore loan accounts have been sanctioned, about two-thirds to women), while PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma support street vendors and traditional artisans," she said.

Last month, the World Bank's Poverty & Equity Brief on India report showed that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, while extreme poverty has been almost eradicated.

Sitharaman said India has witnessed a fundamental shift from temporary relief to removing the barriers that perpetuate poverty. Guided by Antyodaya, the welfare of the last person in the line, the government chose the harder path of addressing deprivations, household by household, ensuring development reached those who needed it most, she wrote.

"There was no magic wand. Each scheme required careful identification of beneficiaries, effective delivery and follow-up until the last household was reached," Sitharaman said, adding, "Prime Minister Modi's sustained attention has helped translate policy into tangible improvements in people's lives.

data.title: Bisleri water scare: What happens when you consume excess bromate and PAHs?
data.description:
A sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water has been declared unsafe by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) after laboratory tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), a group of chemicals that includes several known carcinogens.
 
The findings have raised concerns about the safety of packaged drinking water because some of these substances can damage DNA and have been associated with cancer.
 
What are the dangers associated with bromate?
 
Bromate is an inorganic chemical that can form during the treatment of drinking water, particularly when ozone is used to kill bacteria and other microorganisms. When it reacts with naturally occurring bromide ions in source water, it can produce bromate as a byproduct.
 
 
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), bromate concentrations in water treated through ozonation can vary depending on factors such as the amount of bromide in the source water, ozone dosage, pH and other water characteristics.
 
WHO says bromate can cause cancer following prolonged exposure. In its guideline on drinking water quality, the global health agency said the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies bromate in Group 2B, meaning it is possibly carcinogenic to humans. This classification is based on sufficient evidence of carcinogenicity in experimental animals, although evidence in humans is inadequate.
 
Animal studies have found an increased incidence of tumours in the kidneys, thyroid and other tissues following exposure to potassium bromate. Research has also indicated that bromate can cause oxidative stress, a condition in which unstable molecules damage cells, and interfere with DNA, potentially leading to genetic mutations.
 
The WHO's drinking-water guidelines set a provisional limit of 10 micrograms per litre (µg/l) for bromate. The WHO also notes that bromate is difficult to remove once it has formed, making the control of water disinfection processes important. In the Bisleri case, the company said an initial laboratory examination of a sample collected at its Goa facility on September 30, 2025, recorded bromate levels of 12 µg/l, against the prescribed limit of 10 µg/l. This represented a 20 per cent exceedance.
 
However, Bisleri said in a statement that subsequent testing by the referral laboratory and an independent FSSAI-approved laboratory found bromate levels within the prescribed limit.
 
At higher exposure levels, bromate can cause acute poisoning. Health Canada has documented cases involving people who accidentally or deliberately ingested concentrated bromate solutions, often found in hair treatment products. Symptoms included nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Severe poisoning has been associated with acute kidney injury, kidney failure and hearing loss. These cases involved doses vastly higher than those encountered in drinking water and should not be confused with the potential risks from low-level exposure. ALSO READ: FSSAI suspends licences of five nutraceutical firms over safety violations
 
What does the presence of PAHs in packaged drinking water mean?
 
The second category of contaminants flagged by FSSAI in the Bisleri sample is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, also known as polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons.
 
PAHs are a group of more than 100 chemicals formed primarily through the incomplete burning of organic materials such as coal, petroleum, wood and tobacco. They can also be generated when food is cooked at very high temperatures, particularly through grilling and charring.
 
The health effects PAHs vary considerably as not all them are carcinogenic. According to WHO, the risks depend on which compounds are present and the extent of exposure. Some PAHs can be converted by the body's metabolic processes into reactive substances that bind to DNA and cause damage. If this damage is not adequately repaired, it can lead to mutations and potentially contribute to the development of cancer.
 
The FSSAI has not disclosed the concentration or the specific PAH compounds detected in the Bisleri sample.
 
What does this mean for packaged drinking water safety?
 
The Bisleri controversy has also brought attention to the regulatory oversight of India's packaged drinking water industry. In October 2024, the government removed the mandatory Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification requirement for packaged drinking water and mineral water. The BIS mark shows that a product meets the official safety, quality, and performance rules set by the Indian government.
 
In November 2024, FSSAI reclassified packaged drinking water and mineral water under its high-risk food categories to tighten oversight following the removal of BIS requirements.
 
Effective 1 January 2026, a mandatory FSSAI Scheme of Testing replaced the old BIS mechanism. The scheme requires manufacturers to maintain test records and undertake periodic testing through notified, accredited laboratories.

data.title: India EM weight rises 4 pp: Axis lists 3 factors that can sustain FII flows
data.description:
Clocking a sharp trend reversal in foreign institutional investor (FII) positioning, Indian equities attracted nearly $16 billion in foreign equity inflows since mid-October, with artificial intelligence (AI) trade unwinding emerging as the immediate catalyst.
 
This, along with sharp outperformance by India vis-à-vis peers, boosted its weight in the emerging market (EM) benchmark index by 4 pp since October 1 to 14.7 per cent, according to an analysis by Axis Mutual Fund.
 

What gives India an edge?

Given India's diversification - a domestic-demand-led earnings base and lower direct exposure to the AI theme - FIIs returned dramatically to the Indian stock market. Analysts believe that India will continue to remain a safe-haven as AI unwinding continues globally.
 
 
"This FPI buying appears to be a structural shift away from AI and AI-related stocks to India’s diversified market. The trend of FII buying is likely to continue in the near-term," opined Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. 
ALSO READ: 'Remain constructive on Indian equities irrespective of how global markets do'
 
Axis Capital also identified three triggers that positions India in an advantageous position.
 
- Sector mix: India's benchmarks are skewed towards financial services, consumption, industrials and domestic services than in the hardware suppliers at the centre of the AI selloff.
 
- Positioning: FIIs were net sellers in Indian stock markets for two years, selling stocks worth $60 billion. Benchmark rebalancing is now expected to cut net short position on India, which can generate significant buying pressure.
 
- Oil cools down: Any sustained easing in crude prices bodes well for India’s external balance, inflation outlook and corporate margins, which further supports foreign investor buying.
 
AI unwinding with three shocks: investors were no longer simply extrapolating AI demand, but questioning the durability of profits and the returns on an increasingly capital-intensive build-out; second shock was political as Democrats won a decisive victory in the midterms, bringing data-centre electricity costs, water consumption and local permitting into sharper political focus. The result was greater uncertainty over project timelines, grid connections and regulatory approvals. And the final nail was the Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market Crash LIVE: Sensex slumps 900 pts, Nifty below 25,600; Rupee weakens beyond 93/$
 
In the medium term, Axis Capital believes AI infrastructure spending is set to moderate vs. previous projections as "rising financing costs, regulatory uncertainty and doubts over investment returns force a reassessment of capacity plans".
 
India, it therefore sad, may continue to benefit from diversification away from crowded AI exposures for the next few weeks, although a disorderly global selloff could eventually overwhelm its relative advantage (unlikely for now).
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Layoffs and AI fears: 72% of India's tech workers want to switch careers
data.description:
India's technology sector, long regarded as one of the country's most attractive career destinations for its high salaries and global opportunities, is facing a growing crisis of confidence among its own workforce. As layoffs, restructuring and concerns about artificial intelligence reshape the industry, nearly three out of four technology professionals in India say they would switch to an entirely different career if given the opportunity.
 
A survey of 2,958 India-based professionals by anonymous workplace community platform Blind found that 72% would leave their current careers for a completely different profession if there were no financial costs or retraining requirements. 
72% said they would switch to a completely different career tomorrow if it required no cost or retraining. The largest group, 42%, would make the move as long as the pay stayed the same. Only 13% said they are happy where they are.
 
 
While 30% said they would make the switch immediately, another 42% said they would do so if they could retain their existing salaries. Only 13% said they were happy with their current careers and would not consider leaving.
 
The findings point to a growing disconnect between the financial rewards associated with technology jobs and professionals' long-term satisfaction and confidence in the sector.
 
The reluctance to remain in technology is also extending to the next generation. Around 56% of respondents said they would probably or definitely not encourage their children to pursue careers in tech. Nearly one in three, or 31%, said they would definitely discourage them.
 
" The urge to leave was strongest at Intuit (89%), Goldman Sachs (87%), PayPal (87%), Visa (86%), Expedia Group (83%). It ran nearly as high at Oracle (79%), which has reportedly cut about 12,000 jobs in India this year, as well as at Salesforce (79%) and Adobe (78%), where Blind users have reported silent layoffs in India. Even at Meta and Apple, where it was lowest, more than half would switch," the company said in a statement. 
 
The career shift has already shown up on Blind. With more than a month left in the year, posts written in India about leaving software engineering are up 37.5% from all of 2025. For a growing number of India's tech workers, the question is no longer which company to join next, but whether to stay in tech at all.
 
"They don’t want the next generation pursuing tech, either. 56% said they would definitely or probably not encourage their child to go into tech. Nearly 1 in 3 said definitely not. That view holds even at the companies young Indians most want to join. At Microsoft, the largest group of respondents, 67% would steer their child away from tech, and over 50% felt the same at Google and Amazon," said Blind in a release.
 
The survey comes amid continued restructuring across the technology industry, with concerns over job security, changing skill requirements and the impact of artificial intelligence influencing career decisions. 
Blind surveyed 2,958 India-based professionals between November 6 and 19, 2026. Company figures include only companies with at least 10 responses to the question.
 
Healthcare beats software engineering as preferred career choice
 
When asked which profession they would recommend to a young person starting out today, respondents showed a clear preference for careers they believe offer greater long-term stability or are less vulnerable to automation.
 
Medical and healthcare careers emerged as the most preferred option, selected by 34% of respondents.
 
Artificial intelligence and machine learning came second, with 19%, followed by government and public sector jobs at 15%.
 
Other technology roles, including data, cybersecurity and hardware, accounted for 10% of responses. Law and finance also received 10%, while arts and teaching were chosen by 8%.
 
Software engineering ranked last, with just 4% of respondents recommending it as a career choice.
 
Notably, not a single respondent from Google, Meta or NVIDIA selected software engineering as their preferred career recommendation for young people.
 
The preference for healthcare and public sector careers suggests that professionals are increasingly weighing factors beyond salary, including job security, resilience to technological disruption and long-term earning potential.
 
AI creates a career paradox
 
The survey also highlights an interesting contradiction in how technology workers view artificial intelligence.
 
While software engineering received only 4% of recommendations, AI and machine learning emerged as the second-most preferred career path, attracting 19% of responses.
 
This suggests that professionals are not necessarily turning away from technology altogether. Instead, they may be reassessing which technology skills and roles will remain valuable as AI adoption accelerates.
 
The preference for healthcare, government employment and specialised technology functions also reflects a growing interest in careers perceived to offer more durable opportunities.
 
Asked which path they would most recommend to someone starting out today, respondents leaned toward work AI cannot easily replace, or into AI itself. Medicine and healthcare led at 34%, and 15% picked government or public sector jobs. AI and machine learning came second at 19%. In a Blind thread on which profession has the highest earning potential over a lifetime in India, an Apple employee replied: "IAS (civil services) followed by IPS. Earn more than politicians, never get voted out." In another thread, a Cisco employee listed hands-on jobs: "Landscaper. Plumber. Hvac technician. Dentist. Veterinarian. Physical therapist. Nurse."
 
The findings come at a time when businesses are increasingly integrating AI into software development and other functions, raising questions about the future demand for traditional technology roles.
 
However, the survey does not establish that AI has directly caused professionals to consider leaving the industry. Job insecurity, workplace satisfaction, compensation and changing career expectations could also influence these responses.
 
The Blind survey was conducted between November 6 and November 19, 2026, among 2,958 India-based professionals. Company-level figures include only employers with at least 10 responses to the relevant question.
 
Separately, Blind used its AI tool Clair to analyse discussions posted between January 1, 2025, and November 17, 2026, about leaving technology or software engineering for a different career.

data.title: Karnataka to offer free plots, housing aid: Eligibility, benefits explained
data.description:
Karnataka plans to provide 1.5 million free residential plots to landless families and build 100,000 houses in 2026-27, with the housing programme estimated to cost Rs 2,241 crore. 
 
The proposals aim to address the shortage of residential land and increase financial assistance for house construction, particularly for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) beneficiaries.
 
The state Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, took the decisions at its 26th meeting on November 19, according to a statement from the chief minister's office, PTI reported.
 

Bhooguarantee scheme to cover 500,000 sites initially

Under the proposed Bhooguarantee initiative, the government plans to develop 1.5 million residential sites across rural and urban areas. The first phase will cover 500,000 sites spread over around 25,000 acres, at an estimated cost of Rs 1,000 crore.
 
 
The state estimates that around 1.44 million people currently lack residential sites. Of the proposed 1.5 million sites, 900,000 are planned in rural areas, requiring approximately 45,000 acres. Urban beneficiaries are proposed to be accommodated through a G+3 housing model on around 5,000 acres.
 
The government has identified around 23,500 acres of land across Karnataka's 31 districts, which could accommodate around 470,000 sites. The estimated development cost is Rs 20,000 per site.
 
Who will be eligible for free residential sites?
Under the proposed Niveshana Yojane, eligible landless families, including former defence personnel, will receive free residential sites.
 
The eligibility conditions include:
 
  • Each family must hold a Priority Household (PHH) or Antyodaya Anna Yojana ration card.
  • Annual family income must not exceed Rs 1.20 lakh in rural areas and Rs 2 lakh in urban areas.
  • A three per cent reservation has been proposed for ex-servicemen.
 
Proposed reservations include 19.5 per cent for SCs and 7.5 per cent for STs. The government is also considering reservation for Backward Classes.
 
Priority will also be given to senior citizens, widows, widowers, divorced persons, single mothers, persons with disabilities and transgender persons.
 
Fresh applications will be invited through Nadakacheri, Bapuji Seva Kendras, Grama One and Karnataka One centres. Aadhaar-based e-KYC will be used to verify applicants and prevent duplication.
 
The government will also reverify around 580,000 rural applications pending with the Rajiv Gandhi Housing Corporation Limited since 2018. Eligible applicants in the existing list will not be excluded solely for failing to submit a fresh application.
 
Beneficiaries will receive digital ownership documents, while stamp duty and registration charges will be waived for property registration through Kaveri 2.0.
 

Housing assistance raised to Rs 2 lakh, Rs 3 lakh

Separately, the government has approved construction of 100,000 houses under schemes such as Basava Vasati Yojane, Dr B R Ambedkar Nivas Yojane, Devaraj Urs Housing Scheme and Vajpayee Urban Housing Scheme.
 
Under the beneficiary-led construction model, beneficiaries will build houses on eligible land using government financial assistance.
 
The assistance has been increased from Rs 1.20 lakh to Rs 2 lakh for general category beneficiaries and from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 3 lakh for SC/ST beneficiaries. The enhanced amounts will apply only to the newly approved one lakh houses and not to earlier sanctions.
 
Of the 100,000 houses, 68,000 will be in rural areas and 32,000 in urban areas. The allocation includes 17,150 houses for SC beneficiaries, 6,950 for ST beneficiaries and 15,000 for minority communities. The remaining 60,900 houses will go to the general category.
 
The programme will be funded through the existing Budget allocation and phased adjustments to the Housing Department's allocations in subsequent years.
 
(With inputs from PTI)

data.title: CJI Surya Kant recuses from hearing plea related to Supertech projects
data.description:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday recused himself from hearing a plea related to Supertech insolvency and homebuyers' dispute, observing that one of the applicants was personally known to him.

"One of the applicants was incidentally known to me. I will have to constitute a special bench... He is remotely known to me, not my client or my relative, but known to me. Somebody should have been conscious of this fact. Why unnecessarily become a party? the CJI said.

The CJI said he will constitute a special bench to hear the matter.

The development comes after the bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana reserved its order in the matter on November 16.

 

During the earlier hearing, state-owned NBCC, tasked with completing 16 stalled housing projects of debt-ridden realty firm Supertech, had told the top court that it would like to exit if the homebuyers did not want its involvement.

Earlier, the apex court on February 5 upheld a National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) order asking the National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC) to complete 16 housing projects of Supertech Limited.

During the hearing, the top court had observed that its concern was about the homebuyers and also about who would execute these projects.

The top court had earlier come to the rescue of thousands of hassled homebuyers waiting for the delivery of their houses for almost two decades and upheld an NCLAT order asking the NBCC to complete 16 projects.

It had also restrained all the tribunals and high courts from passing any order that could lead to the stalling of the construction work to be completed by NBCC Limited.

The apex court exercised its extraordinary power under Article 142 of the Constitution to uphold the December 12, 2024 order of the NCLAT, asking the NBCC to take over the projects in the interest of homebuyers.

The bench noted that Supertech, according to many homebuyers, had booked around 51,000 houses for delivery during 2010-12.

The bench had directed the NBCC to undertake the projects and complete those expeditiously as envisaged by an expert committee set up by the NCLAT.

The NCLAT, on December 12, 2024, asked the NBCC, a public sector undertaking under the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, to complete the 16 projects, comprising 49,748 homes in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana and Karnataka.

Around 27,000 homebuyers await receiving houses in these projects.

The NCLAT judgment came after the October 1, 2014 order of the top court that allowed the insolvency appellate tribunal to examine and decide a proposal of the NBCC seeking to complete the stalled projects.

The NCLAT had directed the NBCC to "start the process of award of work before March 31, 2025" and ensure the awarding of the contract within a month thereafter. It was also ordered that the construction work for the 16 projects would start from May 1, 2025.

The NBCC had sought to complete the projects, launched in the National Capital Region (NCR), Dehradun and Bengaluru, but the completion of the residential units took a hit owing to a financial crisis faced by the realty major, leading to insolvency proceedings beginning in 2021.

The NBCC had submitted the terms of reference for undertaking the pending projects of Supertech before the NCLAT.

The public sector unit (PSU) had proposed to complete the 16 projects in three phases.

Under Phase 1, it had proposed to complete Eco-Village-2 (Greater Noida), Romano (Noida), Capetown (Noida), Czar Suites (Greater Noida), Eco-village-3 (Greater Noida), Sports Village (Greater Noida) and Eco-citi (Noida).

Under Phase 2, the NBCC, according to its application before the NCLAT, had proposed to undertake Northeye (Noida), Upcountry (Yamuna Expressway), Eco-village-1 (Greater Noida), Meerut Sports City (Meerut) and Green Village (Meerut).

For Phase 3, the NBCC had proposed to undertake Hilltown (Gurugram), Aravile (Gurugram), Rivercrest (Rudrapur), Doon Square (Dehradun) and Micasa (Bengaluru).

The Union Bank of India initiated insolvency proceedings against Supertech under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 on March 20, 2021, claiming more than Rs 431 crore as of January 31, 2021, along with the accrued interest.

data.title: India's private sector activity hits five-month high in November: Flash PMI
data.description:
India’s private sector business activity is projected to rise to a five-month high in November as demand improved and international sales picked up again, according to a private survey released on Monday. 
 
Compiled by S&P Global, the index went up to 56.3, rising marginally from 56.2 in October. 
 
The reading remained above the 50 mark separating expansion from contraction for the 64th consecutive month. It was also the highest since June, when it was 57.1.
 
Demand for private sector goods and services rose at the quickest pace since June, the survey said. 
 
“Survey participants mainly attributed higher sales to favourable market demand and new customer wins. Some stated that demand was stronger in sectors such as pharmaceuticals and healthcare, chemicals, electronic components, metals, power transmission equipment, logistics, financial services, IT and infrastructure,” S&P noted. Some survey participants cited marketing efforts, discounts and better customer service as reasons. 
 
 
Foreign demand also picked up with new export orders increasing at the fastest pace in four months. Goods producers continued to record a stronger increase in international sales, said S&P.
 
The HSBC Flash India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 56 in November from 54.7 in October. The Flash India Services PMI Business Activity Index fell to 55.3 from 55.8.
 
“A softer increase in services activity was largely counterbalanced by quicker growth in factory production, which outpaced that recorded at service providers by a wide margin,” the survey said.
 
Overall private sector employment rose in November but at a marginal pace. For the manufacturing sector, job creation saw the fastest rate in seven months, while services firms reduced their workforce size for the first time in nearly a year, S&P said.
 
“Workforce numbers edged higher, though service providers trimmed headcounts for the first time in close to a year,” said the survey.
 
Cost pressures cooled in November with operating expenses increasing marginally across both the manufacturing and services sectors. 
 
Selling prices rose faster than in October, rising equally across both sectors, according to the survey.
 
“Manufacturing activity gathered momentum, with output and new orders accelerating. The increase in new orders was driven by stronger domestic demand, while new export orders moderated a bit. Services, by contrast, saw a softer performance despite a sharp rise in new export business. Input-cost inflation stayed subdued, while output-price inflation increased modestly supporting margins,” said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC.
 
The flash PMI is an early indication of the final manufacturing, services and composite PMI readings and is based on around 90 per cent of monthly survey responses. The final PMI data for manufacturing will be released on December 1 and for services on December 3.

data.title: How Zaheer Khan-backed Anchor Sports builds cricket's business in Europe
data.description:
Over six months of rapid expansion, Stockholm-based Anchor Sports AB, co-owned by former India fast bowler Zaheer Khan, has built a three-continent cricket portfolio spanning Belgium, Sri Lanka and Canada. Its stiffest commercial test, however, sits in continental Europe, where the group is absorbing early losses to prove franchise T20 cricket can sustain itself without relying on gambling sponsors.
 
Anchor's push comes amid a fresh wave of Indian capital entering European cricket ahead of the sport's return to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. While the higher-profile European T20 Premier League (ETPL), co-founded by actor Abhishek Bachchan across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands with former India captain Rahul Dravid among its team owners, wrapped up its inaugural season in September, Anchor is backing a slower, grassroots-led model on the mainland.
 
 
Its flagship European side, the Antwerp Anchors, finished runners-up in Belgium's inaugural International Cricket Council (ICC)-approved EUT20 Belgium league in June. The franchise has brought State Bank of India (SBI) and Coca-Cola on board as early sponsors, though its owners declined to disclose revenue, expenditure or a timetable for breaking even.
 
Seeded with profits from founder Nagendra Siddoutam's Stockholm-headquartered IT services firm Acumant, a 200-person Microsoft and artificial intelligence consultancy that acquired local technology firm Northprim in December 2025, Anchor remains firmly in investment mode. "At this point there's a lot of burn, but eventually we'll get to profits," Siddoutam told Business Standard, comparing the venture to the IT product company he set up after Acumant. While IT services can generate profits from day one, building a sports property requires upfront capital before earning a return, he said. 
Mr. Nagendra Siddoutam, Founder, Anchor Sports
 
No IPL copy-paste
 
Khan's route into franchise ownership began through a Mumbai padel partner who introduced him to Siddoutam, and firmed up once he learnt that chief executive Faisal Shariff was running the venture. "Faisal and I go back 25 years," Zaheer Khan said, noting that Shariff started out at Rediff around the time Khan began his international career. He wanted to work with people he trusted on a project built to outlast a single tournament.
 
Both Khan and Shariff are wary of importing India's franchise blueprint to Europe. "You can't just copy it as a tournament," Khan said of the Indian Premier League (IPL).
 
Where the IPL could draw on India's economic scale and vast broadcast audience, European leagues must first raise the standard of cricket available to local players, Khan argued. In Belgium, EUT20 rules paired domestic Belgian cricketers with international names such as Martin Guptill, Moeen Ali and David Wiese.
 
Khan credits South Asian diaspora communities for much of Europe's early participation, but expects better facilities, stronger opponents and the Olympic spotlight to broaden the playing base. That thinking also underpins Anchor's proposed mixed-gender T20 competition, Project EQUAL, aimed at drawing new audiences in Germany and wider Europe. "A lot of the stars of women's cricket today grew up playing cricket with the boys, didn't they?" Khan said, adding that the competition is designed to give that informal pathway an organised structure.
 
Shariff, who served as the IPL's first digital director under Lalit Modi, cautioned against chasing short-term spectacle, a real risk in Europe where earlier ambitions such as the Euro T20 Slam collapsed after repeated postponements. "You don't want to start with a bang and end quickly, before you even get a couple of seasons in and the franchise and the broadcaster start making some profits," he said. 
Mr. Faisal Shariff, CEO, Anchor Sports
 
From Stockholm schools to three continents
 
Anchor's franchise network grew out of grassroots work in Sweden, where Siddoutam has lived for more than 16 years and still plays club cricket. Seeing promising players held back by weak infrastructure, the group built an indoor facility in Stockholm, began working with local schools and brought in former India coach Gary Kirsten and former wicketkeeper Kiran More for youth camps.
 
When plans for an under-23 league in Sweden fell through, Anchor pivoted to Belgium's newly announced league, organised by Destino Legends Sports LLC and the Belgian Cricket Federation. In June, it also signed a youth-development partnership with Denmark's governing body, Dansk Cricket-Forbund.
 
Expansion accelerated in the second half of 2026. In August, Anchor acquired four-time Lanka Premier League (LPL) champions Jaffna, rebranding the side Anchor Jaffna Kings as it finished runners-up in the 2026 final. A month later, Khan joined the ownership group of Anchor's men's and women's Vancouver Anchors franchises in Canada's Super 60 league, reuniting with former India teammate Yuvraj Singh, a stakeholder in the competition.
 
The diaspora bridge and the betting risk
 
Commercially, Anchor's pitch shifts by market. In Test-playing Sri Lanka, cricket needed little introduction. In Antwerp and Vancouver, diaspora demographics offered the starting point. "You go to Antwerp, you feel like you're in Gujarat, to be honest. You go to Vancouver, you feel like you're in Punjab," Siddoutam said.
 
That community footprint helped bring SBI on board in Antwerp. Coca-Cola, announced as an official Antwerp Anchors sponsor in June, required a different approach because its Belgian business knew little about cricket.
 
"Over the next five to six years, Siddoutam wants local European companies and multinationals with sizeable operations in India, such as Sweden's Ericsson and IKEA, to anchor sponsorship revenue. Just as crucially, he wants betting sponsorships kept to a minimum, warning that young leagues risk distorting their finances by chasing quick gambling cash before building a local market.
 
That caution tracks a sharper regulatory squeeze across global sport. According to an October 2026 preview of SportBusiness's Global Betting Report, gambling and gaming firms continue to pour billions into sports sponsorship and advertising worldwide, backing major European properties including Italy's Serie A and Germany's Bundesliga, even as governments and governing bodies curb their visibility.
 
English Premier League clubs have given up front-of-shirt gambling sponsorships, Italy has imposed a sponsorship ban that operators have sought to sidestep through 'infotainment' brands, and Australia has legislated a phase-out running to 2031. In the starkest warning yet for sports properties dependent on gambling money, Brazil banned fixed-odds betting and its advertising outright on September 25, 2026, abruptly halting one of the fastest sponsorship booms in global sport.
 
Indian cricket felt a similar jolt closer to home after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prompted Dream11 to exit as the national team's lead sponsor. For a challenger property like Anchor, walking away from easy betting money makes the early burn harder to absorb. Whether local European brands fill that gap will decide if its long game pays off.

data.title: Bulls take a breather! Sensex dives 1,000 pts intraday; a short-term blip?
data.description:
Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty drifted lower on Monday amid a sharp sell-off in global markets and profit taking after a two-day rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex made an intraday low of 82,893.33, down 1,026 points, or 1.22 per cent. Similarly, the 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 309 points, or 1.19 per  cent to touch a low of 25,491.
 
Analysts said that Indian equity markets are likely to remain volatile, with weak global cues weighing on sentiment after a sharp technology-led sell-off in US markets reignited concerns over AI valuations, global risk appetite and the sustainability of the recent rally. 
VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said that markets are witnessing heightened volatility across segments - equity, currency and metals. While globally equity markets are selling off led by an AI rout, India has been outperforming significantly led by fairly valued large-caps. "The dramatic change in the FII stance towards India, rupee appreciation and better-than-expected impressive earnings growth have combined to boost the market sentiments, strongly supported by fundamentals," he said. 
 
As of 12:40 PM, the BSE Sensex index was down 996, or 1.19 per cent, at 82,923, while the 50-share Nifty traded 300 pois, or 1.17 per cent lower 25,499.
 
India VIX, the fear gauge index, spiked more than 4 per cent to 18.02. This, Sudeep Shah, head - technical and derivatives research at SBI Securities, said that indices increasing nervousness and uncertainty among market participants. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE
 
Stock market crash today: Key reasons
 
Profit booking: Today's sharp fall came after last week's positive momentum. Both the benchmark indices gained more than 2.5 per cent each in the previous week. Analysts said that the a profit booking after last week's rally has dragged the indices lower. Shrikant Chouhan, head – equity research, Kotak Neo, said that if the index falls below 25,500, sentiment could change, and it may see a quick intraday dip towards 25,350–25,200.
 
Banking stocks drag: The Nifty Bank index was the top drag today. The index fell more than 2 per cent, with 13 of the 14 constituents trading in the red. Heavyweights HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, ICICI Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank fell more than 2 per cent each.
 
"Nifty Bank is likely to enter a phase of consolidation in the near term before resuming its broader uptrend. On the downside, the 63,500-63,400 zone is expected to act as a crucial support area. As long as the index sustains above this range, the underlying bullish structure is likely to remain intact," Sudeep said.
 
Last week's rally was led by banking stocks, with Nifty Bank surging 5.9 per  cent (second straight week of outperformance), driven by strong performance from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and SBI.  
Nifty Metal under pressure: The Nifty Metal index remained under pressure for the second straight session today. The index cracked more than 3.5 per cent. APL Apollo Tubes was the top loser, crashing 20 per cent, followed by Tata Steel's 9 per cent decline. 
 
Technical view: According to SBI Securitis, Nifty has witnessed a sharp rally over the past few weeks, resulting in a significant gap between the index and its short-term moving averages. Additionally, the daily RSI is approaching the overbought zone under RSI range-shift principles. Therefore, the index may enter a phase of consolidation in the near term before resuming its broader uptrend.
 
In terms of key levels, the 25,540-25,500 zone remains a crucial support area for Nifty. As long as the index sustains above this range, the short-term bullish bias is likely to remain intact. On the upside, 26,100 will act as the immediate hurdle, followed by the all-time high level of 26,373.
